newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada gas firms say Pan-Alberta in conflict.
newsitem.headline: Canada gas firms say Pan-Alberta in conflict.

text.p: A group of Canadian natural gas producers that filed a lawsuit against gas aggregator Pan-Alberta Gas Ltd claim the company may have breached its arm's-length relationship with indirect owner NOVA Corp, a source from within the producer group said on Tuesday.

"The overall sense is that gas from the pool was used in some cases to NOVA's benefit, rather than the producers'," said the source, who spoke on condition of anonymity. "That's the crux of it -- that there may not have been a complete arm's-length relationship between Pan-Alberta and NOVA."
NOVA, which owns 50.1 percent of Pan-Alberta parent firm Novagas Clearinghouse Ltd, operates the main natural gas gathering and transport pipeline in Alberta.
The source said that the producer pool's gas may have been diverted to be used for NOVA's pipeline load-balancing needs instead of seeking the best market netback.

However, the producers believe it is impossible to gauge whether this occurred, and what the lost value was, because attempts to audit Pan-Alberta's records have failed, said John Sparks, spokesman for Gulf Canada Resources Ltd, one of the smaller players in the group.

"The issue, too, is transparency," Sparks said. "The participants in this action are concerned that Pan-Alberta undoubtedly has the answers, but we can't determine how the gas was marketed and to whom it was marketed."
The group, which also includes such firms as Anderson Exploration Ltd, PanCanadian Petroleum Ltd and Talisman Energy Inc, on Friday filed the suit with the Alberta Court of Queen's Bench.
The suit claims the Pan-Alberta breached contractual, regulatory and fiduciary obligations since 1992, robbing producers of the potential value of their natural gas.

NGC Corp, NOVA's 49.9-percent partner in Novagas, revealed in a statement on Tuesday that the producer group was asking for damages of C$5 million and other costs. The action also states that actual damages may exceed C$50 million.
An official with Anderson, one of the producer group's large players, was not immediately available for comment. -- Reuters Calgary Bureau 403 531-1624
